q: How would you score my decision making this season. Be honest. My draft, my everything given the pick. Rank the decisions top to bottom by team. Keep in mind the players available during draft, the bench, the players added, etc
short: Overall a C+: the draft was a solid B+ with a real star core, lineup setting was an A-, but your waiver churn was a D that cost about 560 points net, 9th of 10 teams.
answer:
Caveat first: the data has no draft order or pick numbers, so I judged the draft from your opening lineups on Oct 20 and 21 and what those players have done. Everything else comes from your transaction log and lineup stats. Two weeks is a small sample, so treat this as a grade so far, not a verdict.

Draft, B+. You came out with Anthony Edwards (51.8 FP per game, the best player on your team), Bam Adebayo (43.8), Donovan Mitchell (42.1), Jaylen Brown (40.7), Jarrett Allen (34.2) and Julius Randle (33.8). That is a strong top six. The misses were depth: Norman Powell (26.2 against a 36.0 projection) and Ryan Rollins (23.0) have underperformed, and Darryn Peterson (30.1) is only fine for a rookie. Taking both Edwards and Morant, who are injury risks, was defensible at their price, but it concentrated your risk.

Lineup setting, A-. You left only 111 points on the bench against what was possible, among the lowest in the league. Your actual 3,600 points versus an optimal 3,711 is a small gap, and you have only 1 dead roster spot. This is your best habit.

Waiver and free agent moves, D. You made 11 adds and 9 drops, and the points your dropped players scored elsewhere beat what your adds scored for you by 560. Only Shake and Blake (-755) and Angel Reese (-683, though they lead the league anyway) are worse. Nifty Neighbas (+385) and Creamy Cropmen (+395) got real value from the same free agent pool. Most of your damage was churn for small returns.

Decisions ranked best to worst:

1. Adding Payton Pritchard off waivers on Oct 30 with no drop. +132 points, and he projects 31.6 now. Best move you made.

2. Setting a disciplined lineup every day (111 points lost). Worth more than any single add.

3. Adding Andrew Wiggins for Scotty Pippen Jr. on Nov 2. +36, and Wiggins projects 32.0.

4. Adding Ivica Zubac for Jakob Poeltl on Nov 4. -38 so far, but Zubac projects 35.5 against Poeltl's 31.7, so it should pay off.

5. Adding Alex Sarr for Day'Ron Sharpe on Oct 29. -41 so far, but Sarr projects 36.6 and starts at center. Reasonable.

6. Adding John Collins for Aaron Gordon today. -45 so far and a small upgrade (31.8 against 28.9 projected), but Collins is on your bench, so no gain yet.

7. Adding Quentin Grimes for P.J. Washington on Oct 28. -66. Grimes is at 16.2 per game, the lowest on your roster.

8. Adding Washington for Toumani Camara on Oct 20. -72, and then you dropped Washington a week later.

9. Adding Scotty Pippen Jr. for Bobby Portis on Oct 23. -119, and Pippen was gone nine days later.

10. Adding Precious Achiuwa and then dropping him for Gordon on Oct 30. -149. Achiuwa scored 223 for others after you dropped him.

11. Adding Portis for Julian Champagnie on Oct 20. -198, your worst move. Champagnie scored 218 after you dropped him, and Portis scored 20 for you before you dropped him too.

Pattern: you keep dropping a player who is already producing for a name you like more. Several of your worst moves were drops of players who then scored 150 or more elsewhere. The fix is to hold production and only chase when the gap is clear.

Injuries are mostly bad luck: 642.8 points lost, including 310.8 from Edwards (6 games) and 124.8 from Morant (4 games). One thing within your control: Jarrett Allen is OUT but sits on the bench while both IR spots are used by Edwards and Morant. That wastes an active spot until one of them returns.

Where you stand: 1-1, 8th of 10 in points scored (3,564), and 9th of 10 in projected power (393.9 against the leader at 465.4). That is fixable. You have the stars to win, and with more patience on the wire this goes from a C+ to a B+ quickly.

moves.do: Stop churning: only drop a producing player when the replacement projects at least 5 FP per game better
moves.why: Your 11 adds and 9 drops netted -560 points, and players you dropped (Champagnie 218, Achiuwa 223, Portis 164) out-scored the adds.

moves.do: If you want one swap, consider Mikal Bridges (free agent, 32.8 projected) over Quentin Grimes (28.1 projected, 16.2 season average)
moves.why: Bridges is about 4.7 FP per game better, the only swap that clears the bar. Check the center cap first, since ESPN rejected an earlier add for too many centers (max 4).
